drcTMB fits nonlinear dose-response models by maximum likelihood with the
[Template Model Builder (TMB)](https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp). The interface
resembles `drm()` of the drc package, but TMB's automatic differentiation and
Laplace approximation extend the models well beyond nonlinear regression:
random effects, non-normal responses, covariates on every parameter,
correlated residuals and priors, together with effective doses and
benchmark doses for all of them.

## Main features

- **Dose-response models**: log-logistic, logistic, Weibull (two types),
  log-normal, Gompertz, gamma, multistage, Michaelis-Menten, asymptotic
  regression, the hormesis models of Brain-Cousens and Cedergreen, the
  threshold model NEC, the substrate inhibition model of Haldane, and the
  exponential and power models of PROAST and BMDS. All share the parameter
  names b1 to b5 (lower and upper asymptote, steepness, location, asymmetry
  or shape).
- **Response distributions** (`family`): gaussian, lognormal, binomial,
  beta-binomial, poisson, negative binomial, beta, and time-to-event data
  (germination counts in time intervals).
- **Covariates** on any of the parameters (`fform`), e.g. one ED50 for each
  treatment, and links of single parameters (`parlink`) or of the whole curve
  (`curvelink`).
- **Random effects** on any of the parameters (`rform`), with correlated
  random intercepts and slopes and nested grouping factors, as in lme4.
- **Correlated residuals and variance functions** (`correlation`,
  `variance`): AR(1), continuous-time AR(1), compound symmetry and spatial
  structures; power, exponential and stratified variances, as in nlme.
- **Inference**: Wald, profile likelihood and parametric bootstrap
  intervals; likelihood ratio, F and bootstrap tests with `anova()`; robust
  (sandwich) standard errors, also for clustered data; confidence and
  prediction intervals with `predict()`; residual diagnostics with `plot()`.
- **Effective doses** (`ed()`) and the **peak** of hormesis curves
  (`peak()`), for every curve of a model, with simultaneous intervals and
  ratios of effective doses through multcomp and mratios.
- **Benchmark doses** (`bmd()`): excess and additional risk, relative
  deviation and standard deviation definitions, also with random effects;
  model averaging with AIC or BIC weights and bootstrap BMDLs (`bmdma()`).
- **Bayesian benchmark doses**: priors on all parameters and on the BMD
  itself, marginal likelihoods and Bayesian model averaging (`bmdbayes()`),
  and the default approach of EFSA (2022) in a single call (`bmdefsa()`).

## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("daniel-gerhard/drcTMB")
```

The examples below use data sets of drcTMB, most of them from the package
[drcData](https://github.com/DoseResponse/drcData), and of nlme.

## A first model

The root length of ryegrass decreases with the concentration of ferulic
acid. A log-logistic model with the lower asymptote b1 fixed at 0 and without
the asymmetry parameter b5 is the three-parameter model `LL.3()` of drc.

```{r ryegrass}
library(drcTMB)
library(ggplot2)
data(ryegrass)

mod <- drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic",
              start = c(b1 = 0, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE))
mod
```

`predict()` gives confidence intervals for the mean response, and with
`interval = "prediction"` prediction intervals for new observations.

```{r ryegrass-plot}
nd <- data.frame(conc = exp(seq(log(0.5), log(30), length.out = 100)))
nd <- cbind(nd, predict(mod, newdata = nd, interval = "confidence"))
ggplot(nd, aes(x = conc)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit), colour = "blue") +
  geom_point(data = subset(ryegrass, conc > 0), aes(y = rootl)) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Concentration of ferulic acid (log scale)", y = "Root length (cm)") +
  theme_bw()
```

Effective doses, here the concentrations that reduce the root length by 10%,
50% and 90% of the range of the curve, come with profile likelihood intervals
by default.

```{r ryegrass-ed, message = FALSE}
(eds <- ed(mod, respLev = c(10, 50, 90)))
confint(eds)
```

## Several curves and a binomial response

The immobility of daphnids was recorded after 24 and 48 hours. A binomial
model with a separate steepness b3 and location b4 for each time compares the
two curves; the asymptotes are fixed at 0 and 1, and the ED50s start at a dose
of 1000.

```{r daphnids}
data(daphnids)
dmod <- drmTMB(cbind(no, total - no) ~ dose, data = daphnids,
               model = "loglogistic", family = "binomial",
               fform = b3 + b4 ~ 0 + time,
               start = c(b1 = 0, b2 = 1, b4 = 1000, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b2 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE))

nd <- expand.grid(dose = exp(seq(log(50), log(22000), length.out = 100)), time = c("24h", "48h"))
nd$fit <- predict(dmod, newdata = nd)
ggplot(daphnids, aes(x = dose, y = no/total, colour = time)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(data = nd, aes(y = fit)) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Dose (log scale)", y = "Proportion of immobile daphnids", colour = "Time") +
  theme_bw()
```

`ed()` estimates the effective doses of each curve given in `newdata`, with
their covariance matrix, so that simultaneous intervals for differences
(`multcomp::glht()`) or ratios (`mratios::gsci.ratio()`) follow, here the
relative potency of the ED50 after 24 hours to the one after 48 hours.

```{r daphnids-ed}
(ed50 <- ed(dmod, respLev = 50, newdata = data.frame(time = c("24h", "48h"))))
mratios::gsci.ratio(coef(ed50), vcov(ed50), rbind("24h/48h" = c(1, 0)), rbind(c(0, 1)))
```

## Random effects

In the PBG experiment of the nlme package, five rabbits received increasing
doses of phenylbiguanide, once after an antagonist (MDL 72222) and once after
a placebo, and the change of the blood pressure was recorded. Random effects
of the rabbits on the upper asymptote b2 and on the ED50 b4 account for the
repeated measurements of the same rabbits; with a log link of b4, the
treatment acts multiplicatively on the ED50.

```{r pbg}
data(PBG, package = "nlme")
pbg <- as.data.frame(PBG)
pbg$Rabbit <- factor(pbg$Rabbit, ordered = FALSE)
pmod <- drmTMB(deltaBP ~ dose, data = pbg, model = "loglogistic",
               fform = b4 ~ Treatment, rform = b2 + b4 ~ 1 | Rabbit, parlink = c(b4 = "log"),
               start = c(b5 = 0), fix = c(b5 = TRUE))
summary(pmod)
```

`predict()` gives the curves of the rabbits and, with `random = FALSE`, the
population curves.

```{r pbg-plot}
nd <- expand.grid(dose = exp(seq(log(6.25), log(200), length.out = 100)),
                  Treatment = levels(pbg$Treatment), Rabbit = levels(pbg$Rabbit))
nd$fit <- predict(pmod, newdata = nd)
nd$pop <- predict(pmod, newdata = nd, random = FALSE)
ggplot(pbg, aes(x = dose, y = deltaBP, colour = Rabbit)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(data = nd, aes(y = fit)) +
  geom_line(data = subset(nd, Rabbit == "1"), aes(y = pop), colour = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ Treatment) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Dose of phenylbiguanide (log scale)", y = "Change in blood pressure (mm Hg)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The standard errors of effective doses and benchmark doses include the
variation between the rabbits. The antagonist shifts the ED50 by a factor of
about two:

```{r pbg-ed}
(ed50p <- ed(pmod, respLev = 50, newdata = data.frame(Treatment = levels(pbg$Treatment))))
mratios::gsci.ratio(coef(ed50p), vcov(ed50p), rbind("MDL/Placebo" = c(1, 0)), rbind(c(0, 1)))
```

## Benchmark doses

The benchmark dose (BMD) is the dose at which the response has changed from
the response at dose zero by the benchmark response; the BMDL, the lower limit
of a 90% interval, is the reference point of a risk assessment. For a 5%
decrease of the root length of ryegrass:

```{r bmd, message = FALSE}
confint(bmd(mod, bmr = 0.05, def = "relative"), level = 0.9)
```

As the BMD depends on the model, `bmdma()` averages it over several models,
here log-logistic and Weibull models with a normal or lognormal response,
with a bootstrap BMDL.

```{r bmdma, message = FALSE}
fitm <- function(model, family = "gaussian")
  drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = model, family = family,
         start = c(b1 = 0, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE))
bmdma(LL = mod, W1 = fitm("weibull1"), W2 = fitm("weibull2"),
      LLlognormal = fitm("loglogistic", "lognormal"),
      bmr = 0.05, def = "relative", nsim = 200, seed = 1, progress = FALSE)
```

`bmdefsa()` follows the Bayesian model averaging of EFSA (2022), with its
default priors, and `bmdbayes()` averages models with priors of your own.

## Hormesis

Low concentrations of isobutyl alcohol stimulate the growth of lettuce. The
Brain-Cousens model adds a hormesis effect b5 to the log-logistic curve, and
`peak()` estimates the dose and the response at the maximum.

```{r lettuce}
data(lettuce)
hmod <- drmTMB(weight ~ conc, data = lettuce, model = "braincousens")
peak(hmod)
```

## Time-to-event data

Germination experiments count the seeds that germinate in each time interval.
With `family = "event"`, each row is an interval from `start` to `end`, and the
curve is the cumulative proportion of germinated seeds. `ed()` then gives the
times by which a percentage of the germinating seeds has germinated.

```{r chickweed}
data(chickweed)
gmod <- drmTMB(count ~ start + end, data = chickweed, model = "loglogistic", family = "event",
               start = c(b5 = 0), fix = c(b5 = TRUE))
ed(gmod, respLev = c(10, 50, 90))
```

## Robust standard errors

If the variance is misspecified, or the observations are correlated within
clusters, sandwich standard errors are available through the argument `vcov.`
of `summary()`, `confint()`, `predict()`, `ed()` and `bmd()`, e.g. for
clusters given by a variable `plate`:
`ed(fit, 50, vcov. = function(f) vcovrobust(f, cluster = ~ plate))`.

```{r robust}
ed(mod, respLev = 50, vcov. = vcovrobust)
```
